paragraphs: Okay, friend, here's the big idea. God is holy, and the people who stand closest to Him get handled with extra care. The priests present "the food of your God," so God says, "He shall be holy to you, because I the LORD am holy—I who set you apart" (Leviticus 21:8). Notice who does the setting apart. The holiness starts with Him, and the priest is just asked to carry it well.

Now, I know the second half of this passage is a tough one. A descendant of Aaron with a defect could not approach the altar, and I think that lands hard on a lot of hearts. But look at what the text also says: he "may eat the most holy food of his God as well as the holy food" (Leviticus 21:22). He's still family, and he still has a place at the table. The text gives the reason for the limit too: "For I am the LORD who sanctifies them" (Leviticus 21:23).

So what does this mean for you, baker? God cares about how His people live, and He cares about the places where He meets them. He is the One who sets people apart, and He says so again and again in this passage: "I am the LORD who sanctifies him" (Leviticus 21:15). Hold the call to holiness with a steady hand, because the One who calls is the One who makes it happen. And the teaching isn't done yet, so keep your apron on!
